summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following his third transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure targeting residual tumors in liver segments VI, VII, and VIII. The procedure was successfully performed via the right femoral artery, delivering doxorubicin-eluting beads to the tumor sites. A previously suspected phrenic artery supply was not identified, but a feeding vessel from the right adrenal/intercostal artery was successfully coiled and embolized to prevent non-target perfusion. The patient tolerated the procedure well, with no immediate complications, pain, or bleeding at the access site. He remained stable throughout the admission, with mild expected changes in liver enzymes. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor for post-embolization syndrome, continue all home medications, and follow up with oncology and hepatology in four weeks for imaging and treatment reassessment.
